text:
Sam B: Heads-up — customer reported spike in p95/p99 for text-generation endpoints around 09:12 UTC. Investigating, but initial look shows KV/prefix cache miss rate jumped ~4x. Anyone seen related alerts?

Anya L: saw the alert from monitoring-bot. p95 went from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s -> 2.6s. Origin looks like increased backend time after cache misses.

monitoring-bot: alert: route=/v1/generate model=redwood-7b p95 latency increased 250% (09:11:40 UTC). kv_cache_hit_rate dropped from 0.93 -> 0.62 in last 10m.

Kevin T: adding logs — on the node serving shard-12 the prefix cache eviction rate spiked. Evictions_per_min went from 30 -> 480. Looks like thrash.

Maria S: Is this correlated with recent deploy? I rolled the kv-cache eviction tuning change yesterday to be more aggressive (shorter TTL) to free memory. Maybe that's the trigger.

Devon P: I remember the change — reduced default prefix TTL from 5m -> 30s for some workloads. That could cause hot prefixes to be evicted prematurely and cause regen storms.

Sam B: Good catch. Can we confirm whether high cardinality keys are also in play? Monitoring shows unique_cache_keys for shard-12 jumped 12x.

Kevin T: Query results (PromQL):
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)
kv_cache_hit_rate{shard="shard-12"}
```
Outputs attached in telemetry: eviction spike aligns with an unusual traffic pattern — many requests with slightly different prefixes.

Anya L: digging into request samples — noticed a bug in our cache key normalization where the `conversation_id` was accidentally included for one of the new SDK query params when `enable_prefetch=true`. That makes keys almost unique per request.

Maria S: oh damn. That would absolutely bust cache. Which PR introduced that param change?

Devon P: PR #4382 touched prefix-key formatting. It added `ctx.session_id` into the key in a conditional branch. I thought the intention was to include only `model+prompt_prefix+user_lang` but the guard was wrong.

Sam B: If that's the case, then immediate mitigation options:
- revert the PR (fast but heavier rollback)
- hotpatch normalization to strip session_id from cache key (small fix)
- temporarily increase TTL and reduce eviction aggressiveness to give cache time to warm
- pre-warm top prefixes for affected models

Kevin T: I'm in favor of small hotpatch + TTL increase. Revert is last-resort. I can roll a patch to sanitize keys and push to canary in 10m. Also propose setting `prefix_ttl` from 30s -> 5m for shard-12 and shard-14 as emergency mitigation.

Anya L: I'll draft a small change to prefix hashing: ensure we only hash these fields: `model_name`, `prefix_text_normalized`, `prefix_len_bucket`, `tenant_id` (if present). Strip `session_id`, `request_id`, `timestamp`.

Devon P: test plan: unit test for key normalization + integration smoke on canary. Also add a high-cardinality detector to raise a warning if unique keys / qps > X.

monitoring-bot: note: runbook step executed: increased prefix_ttl for shard-12 (devops user) at 09:25 UTC. TTL=300s.

Maria S: After the TTL bump, kv_cache_hit_rate recovered to ~0.88 in ~6 mins and p95 dropped to ~150ms. p99 still at ~700ms but trending down. Good sign.

Sam B: Great. Kevin, proceed with hotpatch. Once hotpatch is in canary and validated, we can roll to global. Keep the TTL bump for 1 hour then reassess.

Kevin T: Hotpatch rolled to canary at 09:34. Validation: 5000 requests replayed against canary — unique_cache_keys stable, hit rate ~0.91. No increased CPU.

Anya L: pushing the PR now: title "normalize: exclude transient ids from prefix cache key" — small code change, added unit tests and a quick e2e that replays mixed session IDs.

Devon P: After canary looks good, we should deploy a guard in runtime: if unique_cache_keys / qps > 3 for >2m, automatically pause eviction aggressiveness and increase TTL. Helps prevent future thrash while we patch.

Sam B: Agree. Add this as a short-term policy and file a ticket for longer-term: sticky-prefix routing and better pre-warm heuristics.

Maria S: Customer update: sent a note saying we've identified cause (cache key bug + aggressive TTL), implemented emergency mitigations, and hotpatch in progress. ETA for full fix ~ 1-2 hours. They replied :thumbsup:.

Kevin T: Postmortem action items I'm adding:
- revert aggressive TTL change unless justified (owner: Maria)
- add key-normalization unit tests and fuzzing harness (owner: Anya)
- implement high-cardinality alert and auto-safeguard (owner: Devon)
- add dashboard showing unique_cache_keys / minute per shard (owner: Kevin)

Sam B: Thanks team. Keep updates here. If anyone sees p99 jump after we roll globally, ping infra-oncall and escalate.

ops-bot: deployment: hotpatch-prefix-normalization rolled to global at 10:05 UTC (user=kevin). No rollback triggered.

Kevin T: After global roll, hit rate stabilized ~0.92, p95 ~130ms, p99 ~220ms. I’ll keep metrics on a 30s cadence for 1h.

Anya L: PR merged. Will open follow-up for sticky routing and pre-warm.

Sam B: Closing thread once we verify 1h stable. Great triage and quick mitigation — excellent work. :clap:
